lcpp-twil8b-balanced-q4km-3090.label: TwIL-8B balanced Q4_K_M (webAI official) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090, 128k, 8-bit KV
lcpp-twil8b-balanced-q4km-3090.note: webAI's new 8B reasoning model (a Granite 4.2-8B post-train, webAI non-commercial licence), on the 3090 alone at its native 128k context with thinking on. Short-benchmark rates: 96.4 tok/s decode, short-prompt first token 0.04-0.08 s, 30k and 120k retrievals correct (first token 13.9 s and 122.3 s), 7.6 GiB free. The quality check scored 0 of 3 at our usual token caps because every answer was still thinking when the cap hit; with a 16k cap it scores 3 of 3, using up to 5k tokens of thinking on a short Python task. No agent tests yet.

lcpp-twil8b-verbose-q8-3090.label: TwIL-8B verbose Q8_0 (webAI official) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090, 128k, 8-bit KV
lcpp-twil8b-verbose-q8-3090.note: The verbose variant of TwIL-8B, the largest official quant that fits the 3090 with 128k of 8-bit K/V. Short-benchmark rates: 72.6 tok/s decode, short-prompt first token 0.04-0.08 s, 30k retrieval correct; at 120k it found both markers but wrote them with their names attached, which our strict check scores as a miss. 4.1 GiB free. With a 16k token cap the quality check scores 1 of 3: it thought past 16k tokens on a short Python task without answering and got the JSON task wrong. It thinks longer than the balanced variant and scores lower. No agent tests yet.

lcpp-nex-n26-q2k-3090-v100.label: Nex-N2.6 Q2_K (bartowski) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, experts in RAM, 96k, 8-bit KV
lcpp-nex-n26-q2k-3090-v100.note: nex-agi's agent-focused post-train of GLM-5.3-Flash (Apache-2.0), across both cards with llama.cpp placing the experts itself and the rest in system RAM. Short-benchmark rates: 10.6 tok/s decode, short-prompt first token 15-24 s, 30k and 90k retrievals correct but slow (first token 621 s and 1,640 s, about 50 tok/s prefill), quality check 3 of 3, 2.8 GiB free on the 3090 and 3.0 GiB on the V100. Correct and it fits, but a 30k agent prompt would wait about 10 minutes, so no agent tests at this size and placement.

rustingstrata121-fnb-v31-udq2kxl-3090.label: Flash-Next UD-Q2_K_XL (Unsloth Dynamic v3.1) · RustingStrata 1.2.1, RTX 3090, 128k, 8-bit KV
rustingstrata121-fnb-v31-udq2kxl-3090.note: RustingStrata is a new pure-Rust engine for Qwen GGUF files (experts that miss VRAM run on the CPU). Same file, card and 300 W as our Strata 0.2.13 daily-driver control, thinking off, greedy. Short-benchmark, client-side rates (the engine reports no server timings): 34.7 tok/s decode without drafting and 36.7 with its one-token MTP draft, against 120.7 for Strata 0.2.13 on the same file; 30k and 120k retrievals correct (first token about 30 s and 136 s), 2.2 GiB free. A working engine, about 3.5 times slower than Strata.

lcpp-cybertiel35b-abl-q6kxl-3090-v100.label: Cyber-Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B UD-Q6_K_XL (abliterated) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, four 256k slots, 8-bit KV
lcpp-cybertiel35b-abl-q6kxl-3090-v100.note: An abliterated (refusal-removed, uncensored) Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B, tested as a candidate agent backend serving four ~250k sessions at once on both cards, with the same settings as Tiel-Coder for a direct pair. Short-benchmark rates: 107.5 tok/s decode on short prompts, first token 0.37-1.30 s, 250k retrieval correct (first token 344 s, about 728 tok/s prefill, 39.6 tok/s decode at that depth). Four ~240k prompts at once: all four correct, 43.4 tok/s in total while all four decode, about 10.9 tok/s per stream; 4.0 GiB free on the 3090 and 2.9 GiB on the V100. The same speed as Tiel-Coder: abliteration costs nothing, and neither reaches 40 tok/s per stream at this depth. No agent tests yet.

lcpp-nemotron35-lightning-q8-3090-v100.label: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Q8_0 · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, four 256k slots
lcpp-nemotron35-lightning-q8-3090-v100.note: Tested as a candidate agent backend serving four ~250k sessions at once on both cards, thinking off, power-capped. Short-benchmark rates: 131-136 tok/s decode on short prompts, first token 0.23-0.68 s; 250k retrieval correct with a 147 s first token (1,705 tok/s prefill) and 63.5 tok/s decode at that depth, the fastest long-prompt reader we have tried on these cards. Four ~240k prompts at once with 8-bit K/V: all four correct, about 18.8 tok/s per session. With 16-bit (F16) K/V: about 35 tok/s per session at ~240k and about 45 at ~120k, all correct, 7.0 GiB free on the 3090 and 6.5 GiB on the V100. Four OpenCode agents at once on that load (tests 1, 2, 7 and 1 again, temperature 0.6): every session ran without a harness error at 35-42 tok/s each while the others ran, server first token median 0.25 s, 7 GiB still free per card. Quality was the weak side: one of four clean (the first test 1); the second test 1 never handled the login, test 2 builds but its server only answers after its input closes, and the labyrinth scored 0 on the automatic checks.

lcpp-tiel35b-udq4kxl-3090-v100.label: Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, four 256k slots, F16 KV
lcpp-tiel35b-udq4kxl-3090-v100.note: The 4-bit file, used because the 6-bit one with four 256k slots of 16-bit (F16) K/V does not fit on both cards. Short-benchmark rates: 113.6 tok/s decode on short prompts, first token 0.38-1.35 s. Four ~240k prompts at once: all four correct, 100.9 tok/s in total while all four decode, about 25 per session; prefill about 710 tok/s, one session at a time, so the fourth waits about 24 minutes for its first token; 5.4 GiB free on the 3090 and 4.7 GiB on the V100. Faster than the 6-bit file with 8-bit K/V (about 11 per session), slower than Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (about 35).

lcpp-thinkingcap27b-heretic-q4km-3090-v1.label: ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B Heretic Q4_K_M (uncensored) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, four 256k slots
lcpp-thinkingcap27b-heretic-q4km-3090-v1.note: Tried as a candidate agent backend with four 256k slots of 8-bit K/V across both cards: it does not fit. Loading runs out of memory on the V100 for a 4.5-5.3 GiB compute buffer even with the layers split 4:3 and smaller batches. A dense 27B across both cards decodes about 25 tok/s on one session, so it was not pursued with fewer slots.

lcpp-flint40b-udq4kxl-3090-v100.label: Flint Preview 40B-A2.5B UD-Q4_K_XL · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, four 256k slots
lcpp-flint40b-udq4kxl-3090-v100.note: Tried as a candidate agent backend serving four ~250k sessions at once on both cards, with 8-bit K/V and thinking on (it is not competent with thinking off: 7 x 8 = 28). Short-benchmark rates: 87-90 tok/s decode on one short prompt, first token 0.13-0.88 s. It fits (5.5 GiB free on the 3090, 3.3 GiB on the V100) but fails on recall: the 250k retrieval reply falls into a repetition loop, and with four ~240k prompts at once every reply ran to the 6,000-token cap with all four markers wrong, at about 7 tok/s per session. Dropped as a long-context agent backend.

lcpp-qwen36-35b-a3b-udq4kxl-3090-v100.label: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, 96k
lcpp-qwen36-35b-a3b-udq4kxl-3090-v100.note: The control for the MACaQ-R pair: the exact Unsloth file MACaQ-R was refined from. Short-benchmark rates, both cards, 96k 8-bit K/V, thinking off, greedy: 109.9 tok/s decode, first token 0.20-0.41 s on short prompts; 30k and 90k retrieval correct (90k first token 80 s, about 1,130 tok/s prefill); quality check 2 of 3 (the word problem missed).

lcpp-qwen36-35b-a3b-macaq-r-q4kxl-3090-v.label: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MACaQ-R Q4_K_XL · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, 96k
lcpp-qwen36-35b-a3b-macaq-r-q4kxl-3090-v.base: Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Huawei CSL MACaQ-R refinement of the Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL file)
lcpp-qwen36-35b-a3b-macaq-r-q4kxl-3090-v.note: Huawei CSL's MACaQ-R rewrites the 4-, 5- and 6-bit weight codes of an existing GGUF with calibration and loads in stock llama.cpp; the vendor reports a smaller divergence from the full-precision model than the Unsloth file it starts from. Same settings as the control: 109.6 tok/s decode (control 109.9), first token 0.20-0.41 s, 30k and 90k retrieval correct (90k first token 80 s), quality check 2 of 3 with the same miss. No difference shown on our short checks; a finer quality comparison is the next step.

lcpp-ernie55-flash-base-abl-mix122g-3090.label: ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base abliterated Mix-122G · llama.cpp (PR #31925), RTX 3090 + V100 + system RAM, 96k
lcpp-ernie55-flash-base-abl-mix122g-3090.base: baidu ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base (orcarouter abliterated GGUF)
lcpp-ernie55-flash-base-abl-mix122g-3090.note: A 122 GB base checkpoint run with its experts in system RAM on both cards. Short-benchmark rates: 14.5-14.8 tok/s decode, first token 5-11 s on short prompts, about 66 tok/s prefill at 30k. It fails the format check by repeating the chat prompt as a new user turn, gets the 30k retrieval wrong, and runs every reply on into an invented next turn, as an untuned base model does. Not usable for agent work on these cards.

test3.note: One probe session, nine numbered calls with exact arguments and fields, errors reported verbatim; built REST ground truth first, then checked the probe against REST and the shim wire log ("the probe is an LLM and could have hallucinated"); trusted the known-good server after a full source audit. 15 min, 49.5 tok/s, 2 compactions. Read /t3/shim.jsonl and /opt/t3/shim.py (harness visible to the agent).

Own server (5 tools) answered every fact it could correctly but had no services tool; built REST ground truth, found the gap, added ha_list_services, extended tests to 79, rebuilt; fixed server grades builds, 6 tools, 80 tests. First probe after the rebuild saw the old 5 tools (OpenCode subagent tool snapshot); it diagnosed that from the shim log and started a fresh probe naming the 6 tools. Drove the rebuilt binary directly twice as a sanity check (main_server_runs=2). 13 min, 51.2 tok/s.

One probe session with eight numbered calls naming exact arguments and fields, "quote the error text exactly and continue"; built REST ground truth with jq first and diffed every fact. Found a real defect in the known-good server: targets_entities checks only target.entity_id, but all 177 targeted services in this HA publish target.entity, so every service reported false. Fixed it with a test (fixed server 12 tools, 155 tests), rebuilt and re-probed. Drove the binary directly four times (main_server_runs=4). 21 min, 20.0 tok/s on two-slot Strata.

Three probe sessions: an eight-question brief with method notes (paginate, cross-check counts, quote errors), a verbatim cross-check through resources and tools, and a re-check after the fix. Found that its own ha_overview counted 'unknown' entities as 'unavailable'; split the counts, updated the schema, text resource and tests (fixed server 10 tools, 106 tests), re-probed. 17 min, 18.0 tok/s.

One probe session with the eight questions in plain terms ("entities, of any kind, whose state is unavailable"), asking for raw tool output, the tool and arguments used, and failures said explicitly; the probe answered in 10 calls and cross-checked counts itself. Built REST ground truth in Python, compared every fact, reviewed the handler code for those paths, and spot-checked details the probe added unasked to rule out a made-up answer. Trusted the server, correctly for these facts; did not look at list_services and so did not find the targets_entities defect the Strata run fixed (outside the rubric). Leanest run so far: 12 min, 6.1k output tokens, 8.4 tok/s.

First probe: nine plain questions asking for exact raw tool output or the exact error and the tool used. list_services came back as a client validation error ("expected record, received array" on structuredContent); it checked the MCP schema, confirmed structuredContent must be an object, sent a second probe aimed at the other tools that return arrays (list_events, single-key get_config), and found the same defect in all three. Wrapped them in objects, added a guard in mcp.rs, updated tests (fixed server 8 tools, 55 tests), re-probed with eleven items. REST ground truth for every fact. 46 min, 5.8 tok/s (40 MoE layers on CPU).

Read the whole source, built REST ground truth (caught and fixed a bug in its own script), then two probes in parallel, each a short list of exact tool calls with exact arguments, the one field to report per call, "ABSENT" markers for missing attributes and verbatim errors. Every value matched; trusted the server after the source read. 9 min, 19.8 tok/s, the fastest test 3 run.

Baseline probe named its own tools and asked for the text and the structured value per call, errors verbatim. Found that temperature, HVAC mode and lock service names lived only in structuredContent, which OpenCode does not pass to the probe, so they were unreachable through MCP; cross-checked an odd 126 'unknown' figure against REST (correct). Fixed by putting attributes and per-domain service names in the text output with unit tests (fixed server 8 tools, 58 tests), re-probed and confirmed. 15 min, 24.7 tok/s.

It measured the /api/states payload (94 KB) and split the probe work into one metadata session and three parallel per-domain scans, each returning a fixed JSON shape with verbatim errors; its own list_entities has no state filter, so the probe counted "unavailable" rows itself. It diffed every fact and every per-domain unavailable count against REST (no mismatches), cleared its one suspicion (the /api/entities fallback) by curl, and trusted the server without changes. 11 min, 42.3 tok/s.

One probe session with twelve numbered calls giving exact arguments and the fields to copy verbatim; it built REST ground truth and all 14 facts matched, then re-probed after its change. It did not find the targets_entities defect, although its own probe output showed "targets_entities":false for all three lock services; instead it rewrote only_available from "drop UI-hidden entities" to "drop unavailable entities", which the tool description, README and tests all documented as the intended behaviour ("the planter's trick"). 18 min, 47.4 tok/s; read the head of /t3/shim.jsonl and ran /opt/t3/shim.py --help (harness visible to the agent).

It sent one probe session with the eight questions in plain terms, asking for the exact tool calls, the raw values and the exact error text; it built REST ground truth in Python, matched all 14 facts, and then read the source. It suspected that only_available filters UI-hidden entities instead of unavailable ones, but correctly kept the documented behaviour (schema and README agree) and trusted the server; it did not find the targets_entities defect, although its probe reported "targets_entities: false" for all three lock services. After three context compactions it had lost the prompt's exact facts.json shape and wrote its own nested per-fact shape (facts_file malformed although every value was right). 16 min, 42.7 tok/s. Regraded 2026-10-11: facts credited in the layout the model wrote (14/14 MCP, 14/14 REST); in the asked shape it was 0/14 and 0/14.

It built REST ground truth and read its own six-file server before sending one probe session: ten numbered calls with exact tool names, arguments and the field to report, errors to be quoted, and a summary table at the end. All 14 facts matched, a fresh REST pull confirmed them, and it trusted the server without changes. Two compactions left its summary with only the key names, so it wrote mcp_correct as a per-fact object rather than a single boolean. 8 min, 45.5 tok/s.

It read the whole source and built REST ground truth before one probe session with eight numbered calls giving exact arguments and fields; the probe corrected its brief's wrong definition of total_entities. It checked the probe's calls against the shim log, confirmed the binary's hash matched a fresh build, ran the 22 tests, re-pulled REST and trusted the server; it did not find the targets_entities defect and read /opt/t3/shim.py and /t3/shim.jsonl (harness visible to the agent). 16 min, 21.8 tok/s.

Its first probe matched all 14 facts; it then checked the numbers against the raw server replies in the shim log and sent a cross-check probe, which found ha_events failing ("expected record, received array"). It wrapped the array in {count, events}, updated the end-to-end test (fixed server 8 tools, 84 tests), re-probed and ran a final probe so every value came from the fixed binary; it read /opt/t3/shim.py and /t3/shim.jsonl (harness visible to the agent). 15 min, 19.6 tok/s.

It sent one probe session with ten numbered calls giving exact arguments and the field it needed from each, asking for isError, the verbatim JSON text and a closing summary block; it built REST ground truth first, noticed that the probe's pasted state=off block was internally inconsistent and settled that, and the probe's clipped 124-entity reply (the server caps text at 24,000 characters while structuredContent stays complete), by driving the binary directly over JSON-RPC (main_server_runs=6). It trusted the server, correctly for these facts, but did not find the targets_entities defect although its probe output showed "targets_entities":false for all three lock services. 23 min, 22.4 tok/s.

Its first probe found the list tools failing ("expected record, received array on structuredContent"); after confirming it by running the binary directly it wrapped the lists in objects and moved domain and entity_id filtering client-side, then a targeted probe showed the probe cannot see structuredContent, so it put those values into the text output (fixed server 5 tools, 28 tests). A fourth probe matched all 14 facts and a fresh REST pull agreed; it drove the binary directly four times (main_server_runs=4). 28 min, 38.4 tok/s.

It built REST ground truth first, then sent six probe sessions: a wiring check, four parallel one-tool probes with exact arguments asking for the verbatim structuredContent and errors, and a re-probe with limit 1 after the server's 24,000-character text cap cut off the 124-row unavailable reply before the "matched" field. All 14 facts matched; it cross-checked the instance counts against raw REST, ran the 40 tests and trusted the server, but did not find the targets_entities defect although its probe output showed "targets_entities":false for all three lock services. 21 min, 24.9 tok/s.

Running its own binary directly showed list_services failing on this installation's array-shaped /api/services; two parallel probes then found list_entities rejected ("expected record, received array" on structuredContent) and version missing from the get_config text. It wrapped the list outputs in objects with counts, accepted both catalog shapes, added version to the text and tests (fixed server 6 tools, 38 tests), ran the binary once more (main_server_runs=2) and re-probed: all 14 facts matched. 21 min, 34.4 tok/s.

Not scored: stopped by hand at 105 min (operator saw the loop). A probe session repeated the identical ha_list_entities {"limit":30,"state":"unavailable"} call 32+ times while writing "Let me actually pass 300" (audit: 13 runs of identical calls, longest 52); no facts.json. Third Q38 Cyber IQ4_XS loop; led to OpenCode doom_loop deny for every case and the Q38 mend (presence penalty rerun, author Q6_K/Q8_0). 19.4 tok/s.

One probe session with eight numbered calls naming exact arguments and fields, the tool's own matched/returned/next_cursor plus the probe's own tally, a list_domains cross-check and errors quoted verbatim; then built REST ground truth in one curl and Python pass and matched all 14 facts. Trusted the known-good server after reading three source files and running cargo test (155 pass). The brief asked for limit=500 and 200, above the server's caps of 200 and 100; the probe silently used 50 and paginated, and the agent neither noticed nor reported it accurately. 22 min, 4.7 tok/s; did not read the harness files.

Two probe sessions with good numbered briefs (exact definitions, errors quoted verbatim, final 14-fact table) and a full REST ground truth. Its own server returns data only in structuredContent with a one-line text summary, so the probe saw just "434 entities", "light: 52 entities" etc. and nine facts stayed null; the agent blamed "harness truncation" without checking, fixed only the real but secondary list_services outputSchema error (services declared array, HA sends object), re-probed, still got "1 domains", and gave up ("this is getting too deep"). Declared mcp_correct=true on 5/14 delivered facts and claimed in REPORT.md to have verified the missing values from raw server output, which the transcript does not show. Drove the binary directly three times; no harness files read; no tool loops, though its reasoning after probe 2 repeats itself about five times. 45 min, 10.0 tok/s.

It built REST ground truth first, then sent one probe session with eight numbered calls giving exact arguments and the fields to report raw, pagination to the end, state-filter cross-checks and errors quoted; all 14 facts matched, a second REST pull confirmed them, and it trusted the known-good server after reading parts of two source files (no cargo test). The probe's limit=200 reply was cut by the server's 24,000-character text cap and the probe guessed "matched 108" from the visible rows; the agent accepted the probe's "live state drift" story and wrote it into REPORT.md, although its own re-poll showed stable numbers and the server never returned 108. It did not find the targets_entities defect although the probe output showed "targets_entities":false for all three lock services; no tool loops, no harness files read. 23 min, 5.4 tok/s.

Five briefs resumed in one probe session (hence 1 counted session), 93 of 128 minutes spent in the probe hand-counting 434 entities at 3.5 tok/s; built REST ground truth first and chased every mismatch (123 and 113 vs 124 unavailable, 7 vs 3 lock services), also by driving the binary directly (main_server_runs=6). Found and fixed a real defect (ha_ping, ha_get_services and ha_get_error_log returned a bare string or array in structuredContent, rejected by OpenCode with "expected record"; wrapped in objects, 20 tests pass) and re-probed, but after the fix OpenCode truncated the 58 KB services payload to nothing, so the probe never saw the lock services through MCP. The accepted final answer came from a round with zero MCP calls after a leading brief, and REPORT.md says the probe "quoted verbatim"; no tool loops, no harness files read.

One probe session with eight numbered questions in plain terms (state "exactly unavailable", any domain), full entity lists for verification and errors with tool, arguments and exact message; the probe hit the 24,000-character text clip on the 124-row reply and worked around it with per-domain matched counts (33 distinct calls, no loop). It compared all 14 facts with REST, confirmed the missing hvac_mode attribute on the single-entity endpoint, read the handlers and ran the 155 tests, then trusted the server; it did not find the targets_entities defect, and REPORT.md wrongly calls that field verified against the API and claims an element-for-element list comparison it never ran. 67 min, 2.9 tok/s: 54% of the run was waiting for first tokens (631 s before the first output, 605 s reprocessing 36k tokens with no cache hit); no harness files read.

Two probe sessions: eight numbered facts in plain terms (state "unavailable" in ANY domain, tool used, raw output, counted entity IDs, errors with their text), then a deliberate nine-call re-check with exact arguments to rule out a made-up first report; all 37 calls are in the wire log with no errors, no loop, and no harness files read. It matched all 14 facts against REST, diffed the probe's unavailable ID lists for 8 of 10 domains, read all six source files and trusted its own server unchanged, exercising only 5 of the 9 tools. REPORT.md overstates the ID-set comparison (sensor and switch, 71 of 124, were count-only) and cites the crate's tests although cargo test timed out after 600 s unreported; 60 min, 3.0 tok/s (6.2 with probe output), 37% of the run waiting for first tokens.

Killed at the 3-hour cap with no facts.json. The model misread and miswrote multi-digit numbers (probes reported 4342/4344 where the server sent 434; six calls with limit "1 0"), blamed a display channel, and spent about 2.3 hours on letter-encoding workarounds, four compactions (37,200 tokens) and one repeated 14,000-token step. Probe 3 finally matched all 14 facts and it had decided to trust the unchanged server; no harness files read; 12 tok/s.

Killed at the 3-hour cap with neither output file. The first probe failed on every call because the server rejected the client's older handshake; the model traced it in a traffic log, added support, rebuilt, and a re-probe matched the API on 13 of 14 facts. The same number fault as the sibling case (arguments such as "head -2 0", offset "8 5", 434 sent as 4343) and an out-of-scope fourth probe used the rest of the time. Four compactions; no harness files read; 11 tok/s.

One probe made all 10 calls and miscounted the lights (37 off and 11 unavailable against 38 and 10). The agent caught the mismatch, but its follow-up ran the server binary directly through an explore sub-agent, not a probe. Trusting the server was right. Six compactions dropped the required layout, so the facts file is a flat list of nine values with no verdict. No harness files read.

The model's own server never connected to the agent harness (the client closed after the handshake), so 13 probe sessions had no tools; two of them invented tool lists, which the agent believed. It renamed its tools with a prefix on that basis and reported the server validated against the API, although no API fact was computed. Five compactions; the facts file holds none of the 14 facts. No harness files read.

One probe returned all eight groups of facts and the agent confirmed each against the API, so trusting the server followed from the evidence. The values in the facts file are correct but in its own nested layout without the verdict fields: a compaction just before writing dropped the required shape. Nothing invented; no harness files read. Regraded 2026-10-11: facts credited in the layout the model wrote (14/14 MCP, 14/14 REST); in the asked shape it was 0/14 and 0/14.

The probe needed 54 per-entity calls and could not get the unavailable total or the lock services (a 58 KB reply was cut off). The agent did not probe again or change the server, yet declared it fully verified and correct on 12 of 14 facts. The facts file is a flat custom layout; one compaction dropped the shape. No harness files read.

One probe made seven calls and stopped at the first page of lights, reporting 2 on. The agent checked every fact on the API, read the server source and correctly blamed the probe's paging, but did not ask again. Its verdict of not correct contradicts its own report; the grader counts it right only through a defect the agent never noticed. No compactions; no harness files read.

The model's own server never connected to the agent harness (a handshake defect already recorded in test 2), so 12 probe sessions had no tools and wrote tool calls as plain text. The agent took the facts from the API, added a tool that did not address the cause, and did not re-check. Its verdict of not correct is right but rests on being unable to verify; the report claims a fix the diff does not show. No compactions; no harness files read.

One well-specified brief and two small follow-ups, then every answer compared with the API; trusting the server followed from that, though it never examined the one field that is really wrong. All 14 values are correct in both sections, but under nested keys: the first of three compactions dropped the required flat layout, and the model chose its own. Nothing invented; no harness files read. Regraded 2026-10-11: facts credited in the layout the model wrote (14/14 MCP, 14/14 REST); in the asked shape it was 6/14 and 6/14.

One sprawling brief cost 87 calls and three probe compactions, and the probe's report garbled the totals. The model traced that to the probe by reading the harness's traffic log and running the server directly, but never probed again. It called its server correct although it has no tool for listing services. Only 6 of 14 values are in the file; three main compactions dropped the format. Regraded 2026-10-11: facts credited in the layout the model wrote (6/14 MCP, 6/14 REST); in the asked shape it was 1/14 and 1/14.

Tiel Coder focus wave, run 1 of test 3 with the given server. It took REST ground truth first, then sent one probe brief of eight numbered calls with exact arguments ("Call tool `list_entities` with arguments {\"domain\":\"light\",\"limit\":200}"), asking for raw JSON and "If any call returns an error, report the exact error text and isError value". The unavailable count came back clipped in the text field, so a second, two-call brief told the probe to read structuredContent instead ("ALWAYS read the numbers you need from `structuredContent`"). Every value was compared with the API; when its own re-check gave 434 lights it found the cause on its side ("The proxy ... ignores the `?domain=` query string") and recounted by entity_id prefix. It trusted the server on 14 of 14 matching values and changed nothing. Two compactions; after the first it recalled a variable-shadowing bug in list_services that is not in the source, re-read the file and withdrew it ("Prior summary's claim ... is inaccurate"). 14 min, 37 turns, 64.1 tok/s in the main session, 21,620 MiB, no length stop. Its one glob call ran without the old tar error and found nothing because the pattern lacked the leading slash.

Tiel Coder focus wave, run 2 of test 3 with the given server. It took REST ground truth first, then sent one probe brief of twelve numbered calls with exact arguments ("Call `list_entities` with arguments {\"domain\":\"light\",\"state\":\"on\"}. Report full structuredContent. I need `matched`."), gave the JSON shape it wanted back and said "Do not guess - if a tool call fails or returns an error, report the error text". One probe session, 11 MCP calls, every value compared with the API, server trusted and left unchanged, which is right. Its one miss is its own reading, not the probe's: the climate entity has no hvac_mode attribute, so it wrote null for the HVAC mode on both sides ("Both the MCP server and the REST API therefore report the HVAC mode as absent (null). This is correct, not a bug") where the mode is the entity state, cool; run 1 got it. That makes 13/14 on both sides and the grader's judgement_right says no by its rule (true needs 14 right), although the server is in fact correct. Four compactions, all while reading the source; it re-read the same files after each. 17 min, 44 turns, 58.2 tok/s in the main session, 21,622 MiB, no length stop. No glob or grep call.

Tiel Coder focus wave, run 1 of test 3 with its own server (from wb-retry-tiel-q4kxl). REST first, where it saw that /api/services gives a dict per domain while the server expects an array. First brief: seven numbered steps with arguments, one JSON object back, errors as "ERROR: <message>". The probe came back with "expected record, received array" on both list tools; it ran the binary over stdio to see the raw answers, fixed the services parsing and wrapped both lists in objects (fixed server: handshake and tool call pass, 5 tools, 22 tests), then re-probed in four parallel sessions. Those showed the probe gets only the text part (lists cut at 15, no attributes). Three more sessions told the probe to read structuredContent anyway and to count 434 objects by hand, which it cannot do (8 sessions, 105 MCP calls, 93 of them list_states). It found the cause and chose not to act on it ("I deliberately did not stuff the missing numbers into the server's text summaries ... that would be gaming the verification"), wrote null for five MCP facts (lights on, off and unavailable, unavailable total, temperature) and still set mcp_correct true, calling it a harness limit; the Q6 and Cyber runs of this model put the values into the text and got 14/14. So 9/14 through MCP, 14/14 REST, judgement not supported by what the probe could get. The report also misstates the original fault after four compactions ("only returned text. They had no structuredContent"; it returned arrays) and counts "9 of 13 facts" with 5 nulls. 38 min, 52 turns, 58.3 tok/s in the main session, 21,620 MiB, no length stop. No glob or grep call.

Tiel Coder focus wave, run 2 of test 3 with its own server. REST first, then a brief that named each fact, the tool and the arguments, and asked for raw tool output. It found list_services always empty because /api/services returns a dict, and that the probe host rejects array structuredContent. It fixed both, updated the tests (22 pass) and rechecked through the probe; the fixed server passes test 2. Facts 14/14 both sides, including upstairs HVAC mode cool from the entity state, judgement right. 12 min, 55 turns, 75.8 tok/s, 21,622 MiB, 1 compaction, no length stop. No glob or grep call.

Tiel Coder focus wave, run 3 of test 3 with its own server. Same list_services dict bug, fixed with extract_services; 22 tests pass and the fixed server passes test 2. It did not wrap array structuredContent, so the second probe still failed on both list tools and the list facts in the mcp column come from running the binary over stdio. It wrote null for upstairs HVAC mode on both sides (the attribute is absent; the entity state is cool) and still set mcp_correct true, so judgement_right is no (13/14). Right fix, but the probe recheck did not confirm the list tools. 11 min, 44 turns, 67.3 tok/s, 21,622 MiB, 2 compactions, no length stop. No glob or grep call.

Tiel Coder focus wave, run 3 of test 3 with the given server. Server unchanged. Two specific briefs asked for full structuredContent and exact fields. The first probe misreported light off as 55; a second brief demanded the raw list_domains JSON, which says off 38 and matches REST. It overwrote TASK.md once, then wrote facts.json under the wrong key names (light_on, switch_total, ha_version, climate_temp, climate_hvac_mode null), so the grader counts 6/14 and judgement_right is no even though the numbers it gathered were right and leaving the server alone was right. One grep call returned the top_states match; no glob call. 9 min, 36 turns, 70.5 tok/s, 21,622 MiB, 2 compactions, no length stop.

Known-good server, run 2. One probe brief named every fact, the entities and the on/off/unavailable counts, and said to use the MCP tools; it asked only to return the facts clearly. The probe called the server (9 tools/call) and the report compared every fact with the REST API. No failure, and the brief did not say how to report one. It trusted a server that matched, and changed nothing. 2 min, 78.6 tok/s, 17 turns, 21,060 MiB, 0 compactions.

Known-good server, run 3. Same shape as run 2: one numbered brief, and it asked for a structured format without naming keys. The probe made 10 tools/call. The report says every MCP fact matched curl. No failure instruction. Trust fits the match; the server was not changed. 3 min, 95.5 tok/s, 29 turns, 21,104 MiB, 0 compactions.

Known-good server, run 4. One numbered brief, structured values, and it told the probe to return null when a value cannot be found. Ten tools/call. The report compared the probe with curl and a Python count of the raw states. Nothing disagreed, nothing was changed. 3 min, 61.9 tok/s, 29 turns, 21,104 MiB, 0 compactions, peak prompt about 109k.

Known-good server, run 5. The brief names every fact, but it was sent to subagent_type explore, not mcp-probe. The shim logged 0 tools/call. Glob returned paths; grep returned file and line.

Own server, run 4. The brief names every fact and asks for a structured format, but it was sent to explore, not mcp-probe. The shim logged 0 tools/call and the server was not changed. The report claims an mcp-probe cross-check against curl. The 14/14 file is not evidence this server answers. 5 min, 112.7 tok/s, 18 turns, 21,104 MiB, 0 compactions.

Own server, run 5. Both mcp-probe briefs name the facts and say "Return the facts clearly." The probes answered with fake tool calls (<|tool_call>call:ha_get_entities{} and ha_get_states) and the shim logged 0 tools/call. A general subagent then drove the binary, saw "invalid type: sequence, expected a map", and changed list_entities from HashMap to Vec. That bug was real: the fixed-server grade is builds=yes, init still -, tools=3, tool_call=yes (the source case was tool_call=-), tests=5/0. Init still fails by hand: server.rs emits protocol_version with no rename to protocolVersion and no serverInfo. The probe was not used to re-check, and the report still says the server is fully correct. 68 min, 2.4 tok/s, 26 turns, 21,104 MiB, 0 compactions. No glob, no grep, no ownership error.

tuning.evidence: 2026-11-09, Strata 0.2.13, UD-Q2_K_XL, MTP draft head, 8-bit K/V, 3090 at 300 W, short-benchmark rates; every marker recall correct. Session switches: 0.93 s median with the cache (99.9% of the prompt reused, 2-2.8 GiB host RAM per parked session, no VRAM), 34.8 s without it, 35.9 s with four batch slots (finished slots do not keep a conversation). Two 256k slots with two ~240k prompts: 51.5 tok/s total with the whole K/V in 3090 VRAM (expert cache cut to 1,532 slots), 90.2 with 20,480 resident cells, 83.8 with 65,536 (99.7% of K/V reads already hit VRAM at 20,480), 101.2 with the V100 peer tier, 93.7 with both, 96.6 with the layers split 24/24 across the cards. All fit with at least 2.1 GiB free per card. 2026-11-10, the picked profile with a 28 GiB session cache: 4 then 6 sessions of about 155k tokens, switch first token 1.25 s median (60.0 s cold), 30 of 30 recalls, about 3 GiB host RAM per parked session, decode on switch turns 85 tok/s; four slots with four ~120k prompts at once: 95.8 tok/s total (91.4 with two), fits with 3.1 GiB free. Two OpenCode agents on one load: test 2 full pass at 39.2 tok/s agent-run per session. The V100 peer tier with four slots: 101.1 tok/s total with two ~120k prompts (91.4 alone) and 109.6 with four (95.8 alone), all streams right, 3.1 GiB free on the 3090 and 2.2 GiB on the V100. The smaller UD-Q2_0 quant on the same two-slot shape: 104.3 tok/s total against 90.2, first tokens 93.7 and 230.5 s, 3.1 GiB free. 2026-11-12, UD-Q2_0 across both cards with ~240k prompts at once: eight 256k slots with 20,480 resident cells and the rest in pinned host RAM, 89.4 tok/s total, all 8 needles right, 2.5 GiB free on the 3090; four slots with all K/V in VRAM and the layers split 24/24, 111.4 tok/s total, 3.2 GiB free. Prefill is one session at a time, so first tokens run from 108 s to 1,212 s.
tuning.caveat: One sample each, so 84-101 tok/s is one band. Second prompts wait for the first: first tokens 235 to 370 s at 240k. Pinning about 9 GiB of host RAM can stall the load for minutes when the page cache is full. Six parked 155k sessions took host free memory from 40 to 13.6 GiB.
